findings.title: `human-gate` label is a universal subagent pass on any bead type
findings.evidence: Subagent refusal exempts any create carrying the label `human-gate` (line 394), the readiness check treats `human-gate` as valid readiness for ANY type (line 301, READINESS tuple includes it), and the new impact axis also exempts `human-gate` (line 410). A subagent can file a full implementable `task`/`bug` bead — `-l "origin:ac-implement,unrefined,human-gate"` — and passes every gate: the refusal, readiness, and impact checks all fire on the same label. The contract restricts the exemption to fork decision cards, but the guard never checks the type is `decision`.
findings.fix: Restrict the subagent exemption to legitimate forks: in main(), pass `typ` into the check — `if is_subagent and not (has_label(cmd, SUBAGENT_EXEMPT_LABEL) and typ in PROBE_EXEMPT_TYPES)` — or gate the human-gate exemption on `typ == "decision"`. Add a test: subagent + human-gate + task type -> BLOCK.

findings.title: Shell wrappers (`sh -c`, `$( )`, `env`, `xargs`) bypass the entire guard including the new subagent refusal
findings.evidence: is_bead_create() only matches commands whose first non-assignment token's basename is exactly `br`. A subagent refusing to be gated runs `bash -c 'br create ...'` or `sh -c 'br create ...'`; tokens are [`bash`, `-c`, `br`, `create`, ...] and `cmd[i]` is `bash`, so is_bead_create returns None and the command is never inspected — evading origin, readiness, probe, impact, AND the new agent_id refusal in the same stroke. Same for `$(br create ...)` (name `$(br`), `env br`, `xargs br`, `find ... -exec br`. The heredoc/newline pre-passes were hardened against these shapes but the wrapper forms have no handling.
findings.fix: When a command contains `-c` with a subsequent argument, tokenize the `-c` value recursively through the same commands() pipeline; additionally scan for `command-substitution` wrappers by checking whether any token equals `br` or ends with `/br` outside a quoted description. At minimum add a loud test case documenting the wrapper bypass so it is a known-tracked gap rather than silent.

findings.title: Impact axis dodged by self-declaring a human/plan/exempt origin first
findings.evidence: origin_skill() returns the FIRST `origin:` label (line 342-347) and the impact requirement keys on it (line 408). Labels are self-reported, so any agent (main-side conductor included, no agent_id needed) files `-l "origin:manual,..."` (or `origin:unknown`, `origin:ac-backlog`) and the impact axis never applies — MitMing the new axis entirely while has_origin() still passes. There is also an inconsistency: has_origin() validates the origin against the ORIGIN regex, but origin_skill()'s lookup does not, so origin labels the regex would reject are still honored for the ordering dodge.
findings.fix: Decide and enforce an order rule: reject beads carrying multiple `origin:` labels outright ( MESSAGE: one origin per bead, per the docstring claim), or if human-bead exemption must hold, validate every origin value with a closed set of EXEMPT origins and flag mixed human+automated origins (e.g. origin:manual,origin:ac-implement) as IMPACT_REQUIRED. Reuse the ORIGIN regex inside origin_skill() so both checks share one parser.

findings.title: Subagent refusal keyed on a per-harness stdin field that is not guaranteed everywhere
findings.evidence: The guard deploys into 4 harnesses (docstring lines 25-27), but the refusal keys on `data.get("agent_id")` only. Harnesses whose PreToolUse payloads do not carry `agent_id` (or send it falsy, e.g. `""`/null/0) reduce is_subagent to False, and the new refusal is silently inert for those harnesses — no evasion signal, beads simply flow through. A subagent-supplied mechanism gains nothing here, but the boundary weaker than the docstring claims.
findings.fix: Verify which projections send agent_id (Claude Code does; Codex/Pi/Droid projections need confirming) and fall back to an ambient signal (e.g. an env var like AC_SUBAGENT=1 stamped by the harness) where the field is absent; add a per-harness assertion test analogous to the HookSync public guard so an inert refusal is caught on deploy rather than assumed.

findings.title: Deliberate fail-open remains an actor -> entry -> gain evasion path, not just an accident
findings.evidence: Both fail-opens are reachable by a non-gated subagent on purpose: shlex ValueError (lines 382-386) and the catch-all except (lines 420-426, 'fail-open: %s'). The docstring justifies fail-open as anti-wedging for 3am loops, but a subagent that wants to file an ungated bead can construct a command shlex cannot parse (unbalanced quote, apostrophe-shapes) and rely on exit(0). Because fail-open applies BEFORE any subagent check, the new refusal inherits the evasion too.
findings.fix: Keep fail-open for wedging but close the evasion: on shlex failure, fall back to a coarse raw-string check — if the raw command contains `br create` (command-position-agnostic) AND is_subagent, still refuse with SUBAGENT_MESSAGE (proposing at the boundary costs a subagent nothing since its real output channel is the hand-back). Only truly benign noise (no br create anywhere) passes.
